p02-ctx-t.text: **Used on this page**: $g_i=\mathbf{w}_i^T\mathbf{a}$; $\mathbf{w}_i\in\mathbb{R}^{l+1}$, the last entry is the bias; strict condition $g_i>g_j$ (for all $j\ne i$).

p03-title.text: Block vector: one inner product gives the difference of two scores

p03-bridge.name: p03-bridge

style.fontFamily: "Microsoft JhengHei", "Noto Sans CJK TC", "PingFang TC", "Segoe UI", sans-serif

p03-bridge.text: Last page: we compare two scores. This page uses a block vector to turn subtraction into an inner product.

p03-ctx-t.name: p03-ctx-t

style.fontFamily: "Microsoft JhengHei", "Noto Sans CJK TC", "PingFang TC", "Segoe UI", sans-serif

p03-ctx-t.text: **Used on this page**: $\mathbf{v}=(\mathbf{w}_1;\dots;\mathbf{w}_M)$; $\mathbf{z}_{ij}$ puts $+\mathbf{a}$ in block $i$ and $-\mathbf{a}$ in block $j$, zeros elsewhere.

p03-fig-title.name: p03-fig-title

style.fontFamily: "Microsoft JhengHei", "Noto Sans CJK TC", "PingFang TC", "Segoe UI", sans-serif

p03-fig-title.text: Take $M=3$: $\mathbf{v}$ and $\mathbf{z}_{12}$ multiply block by block

p03-c2-t.name: p03-c2-t

style.fontFamily: "Microsoft JhengHei", "Noto Sans CJK TC", "PingFang TC", "Segoe UI", sans-serif

p03-c2-t.text:
$\mathbf{z}_{ij}$: block $i$ holds $+\mathbf{a}$, block $j$ holds $-\mathbf{a}$, other blocks are $\mathbf{0}$
The inner product multiplies block by block; zero blocks contribute nothing: $\mathbf{v}^T\mathbf{z}_{ij}=g_i-g_j>0$
Each sample needs $M-1$ comparisons; $N(M-1)$ vectors in all, each of dimension $M(l+1)$

p03-ban-t.text: Takeaway: a block inner product writes 'class i beats class j' as one positive inner product.

p04-ctx-t.name: p04-ctx-t

style.fontFamily: "Microsoft JhengHei", "Noto Sans CJK TC", "PingFang TC", "Segoe UI", sans-serif

p04-ctx-t.text: **Used on this page**: the failed constraint $\mathbf{v}^T\mathbf{z}_{ij}\le0$; update $\mathbf{v}\leftarrow\mathbf{v}+\rho\mathbf{z}_{ij}$, $\rho>0$.

p04-fig-title.name: p04-fig-title

style.fontFamily: "Microsoft JhengHei", "Noto Sans CJK TC", "PingFang TC", "Segoe UI", sans-serif

p04-c2-t.name: p04-c2-t

style.fontFamily: "Microsoft JhengHei", "Noto Sans CJK TC", "PingFang TC", "Segoe UI", sans-serif

p04-c2-t.text:
$\mathbf{v}\leftarrow\mathbf{v}+\rho\mathbf{z}_{ij}$ is equivalent to: add $\rho\mathbf{a}$ to the right class's weights, subtract the same vector from the rival's
In code, update only the two nonzero blocks; no need to allocate the full high-dimensional zero vector
Every comparison shares one set of class weights, unlike separately trained one-versus-rest
